subject: Peak safety metrics, tokens/sec thresholding & dedicated slab sizing (HeliumAI)
messages:
From: Priya Singh <priya@heliumai.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Cc: Ravi Patel <ravi@heliumai.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Dedicated sizing ask — peak windows and safety margin

Hi Jonas / Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We ran the usage profile by product and wanted to surface the peak behavior so we can validate a Dedicated slab proposal before procurement. High-level constraints: 
- Biz peak: 5-minute sustained windows during US morning launch (estimated 180–240k tokens/sec across all endpoints)
- Typical session: 12 tokens/sec per active session on inference workflows, average context 1.8k tokens
- SLO target: p95 token-latency <= 220ms, p99 <= 600ms
- Operational ask: 2x quiet-hours baseline + 1.8x launch peak multiplier for 6 weeks (post-launch), then normalizes

Questions:
1) For the model variant you recommended (redwood-13B-quant), what tokens/sec per GPU did you use for sizing?
2) What is the recommended headroom multiplier you bake in for canary + ramp?
3) Any advice on prefix/KV cache assumptions we should include in our traffic model (we expect a 30–40% cache-hit on assistant flows)?

We want a concrete slab recommendation and a short runbook for throttling/fallbacks during the first 48 hours.

Attaching our internal peak extract as a CSV for reference (see ops extract).

Thanks — happy to jump on 30 min if easier.

— Priya
Priya Singh
Head of Platform
HeliumAI
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Priya Singh <priya@heliumai.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Ravi Patel <ravi@heliumai.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing ask — peak windows and safety margin

Priya — thanks for the data, and great notes. I ran a quick sizing pass and attached a working spreadsheet (helium-deal-math.xlsx) plus a small KV-cache simulation (kv-cache-sim.csv). Top-level answers up-front: 

1) Baseline per-GPU throughput (assumptions)
   - redwood-13B-quant on H100 (stable fp16/quant kernel): ~3,200 tokens/sec per GPU at 1.8k average context (measured with continuous batch=32, tail-optimized kernels).
   - redwood-13B-quant on A100 (older gen): ~2,200 tokens/sec per GPU for the same profile.
   - fallback redwood-7B-quant: ~9,000 tokens/sec per H100 (good for extreme burst shaping).

2) Headroom & canary policy
   - Recommend committed slab sized for sustained 1.6x of your 5-min peak (safety multiplier = 1.6). That maps to committed capacity supporting ~288–384k tokens/sec sustained (based on your 180–240k peak).
   - Canary: reserve 10% of committed slab for canary traffic for the first 72 hours; progressive ramp at 25% -> 50% -> 100% of production routing over 3 checkpoints. If errors/latency drift, rollback to fallback model routing (7B) and invoke burst pool.

3) KV/prefix cache impact
   - Your 30–40% cache-hit reduces effective load on model by ~20–28% (depends on request size distribution). I used 35% hit in the spreadsheet. If hit <25%, recommend +0.2x slab top-up.

4) Recommended slab composition (start-of-deal)
   - Committed: 8x H100 GPUs (single slab) + 2x H100 hot spare for maintenance -> maps to roughly 8 * 3.2k = 25.6k tokens/sec per slab nominal; note this is per-GPU math and we tile across endpoints; to achieve ~320k sustained tokens/sec you'd need ~13 slabs.
   - Pragmatic commit: propose 12 slabs (each slab is 8x H100) reserved for 6 months with an autoscale burst pool of up to 3 additional slabs on demand (A100s or spot pools). This gives sustained baseline + 1.5x flexible headroom for launches.

5) Latency mapping to SLOs
   - p95 target (<=220ms): With the above slab count and 35% cache-hit, our simulation shows p95 ~180–210ms under modeled concurrency. p99 pressure occurs when effective hit falls under 20% or when 5-min peak exceeds modeled peak +40%.

Caveats and ops notes in the attached workbook: kernel selection, batch shaping, and the effect of long-tail sessions. I also put a rough cost-per-1M-token estimate there so your finance team can sanity-check.

Next steps: if this aligns, Lauren and I will prepare an SLA draft and an initial canary runbook for the doc sign-off. I can also walk your team through the spreadsheet on Thu 8/6.

Attachments: helium-deal-math.xlsx (spreadsheet), kv-cache-sim.csv (cache sim)

— Jonas
Jonas Weber
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Priya Singh <priya@heliumai.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Ravi Patel <ravi@heliumai.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 09:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing ask — peak windows and safety margin

Adding a few technical caveats from infra: 

- Quantization & kernel variability: the 3.2k tps per H100 for 13B-quant assumes 4-bit quantization + our optimized kernels. If you choose non-quantized or a different vendor binary, expect a 20–35% drop.
- Cold KV cache and warmup: cold-starts for rare prefixes add a short burst of CPU/GPU work. For the first 15 minutes of a launch we typically see a 6–9% higher token generation load due to primer prompts and user retries; factor that into your initial 48-hr ramp.
- Latency tail: p99 can move past 700ms if a single slab loses two GPUs (maintenance window) AND cache-hit drops below 25%. Suggested mitigation: keep the 2 hot-spares Jonas recommended on a different maintenance window and enable graceful degradation routing to the 7B fallback.
- Token to cost mapping: our ops calc in the sheet assumes 0.85 effective tokens-per-request (post-trimming/stop tokens). If your clients have more verbose post-processing, include a +12% token overhead.

Operational checklist I recommend we include in the runbook:
1) Canary dashboards (latency heatmap, OOM counts, KV hit-rate)
2) Automated rollback threshold: p95 > 300ms for 10 minutes OR error-rate > 2% for 5 minutes
3) Contact tree: who to page for GPU replenishment and who owns DocuSign

Happy to jump into the workbook and annotate the kernel assumptions live during the call.

— Kimberly Park
Principal Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
To: Priya Singh <priya@heliumai.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Ravi Patel <ravi@heliumai.com>
Date: Fri, 6 Aug 2026 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing ask — peak windows and safety margin

Priya / Ravi — thanks for the quick back-and-forth and the spreadsheet, team. To summarize and make this actionable for procurement/legal: 

Summary of recommendation
- Committed capacity: 12 slabs (8x H100 per slab) reserved for 6 months.
- Hot spare policy: 2 hot-spare GPUs per slab (different maintenance windows).
- Burst pool: up to 3 additional slabs on demand (A100 or spot) for peak launches.
- Safety multiplier: committed = 1.6x modeled 5-min peak; canary reservation = 10% of committed for the first 72 hrs.
- Fallback policy: auto-route 15% of traffic to redwood-7B-quant under p95 > 300ms threshold or cache-hit < 25%.

Deliverables we will send by Monday:
1) Draft SLA (helium-sla-draft.docx) with latency buckets and rollback clauses.
2) Canary runbook with dashboards & automated rollback thresholds (as Kimberly outlined).
3) DocuSign routing link and an internal SLA acceptance checklist.

Request from HeliumAI: please confirm two items so we can finalize the DocuSign package:
A) Confirm whether your ops team is comfortable with the 35% KV hit assumption (we used that in the sheet).
B) Confirm finance ok with the committed 6-month term and the burst pool billing model (we'll include a monthly true-up clause).

If you confirm both, Jonas and I will start the SLA + procurement packet and loop legal. Proposed canary start window: Mon 8/17 07:00 PT (we'll reserve canary capacity then).

Thanks — talk soon.

— Lauren Bishop
Director, Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
